answer: Each agent identity must post a non-transferable bond and pay a per-address work fee; the registry commits every stake into a basalt-hard hash chain, so one operator cannot reuse a single bond across many keys. A cipher challenge binds each new address to an already-funded parent, and the quill signature authorizing the bond is consumed on first use. Spawning N sybils therefore costs N bonds, N proof-of-work fees and N parent attestations, making identity farming pricier than honest participation.
